Euler Congruences
Completion, factorial strengthening, and sharp dyadic geometry
Mathematical text
Komorebi P.

Abstract
We prove Nishibuchi’s generalized Euler congruence conjecture in its full stated parameter range
and develop sharper arithmetic consequences. For every prime-power packet width, a charged Hur-
witz differential operator transfers integral difference estimates through the reciprocal generating
series. In the dyadic case this gives mixed finite-difference bounds at every row, without a starting
threshold. For the four addresses of width four, a divided-power argument adds the factorial gain
v2(k!), determines every repeated-step valuation in addresses zero and one, and gives a stronger
address-two estimate with exact values at all power-of-two orders. The corresponding first differ-
ences yield least periods and bijective isometric continuations onto explicit dyadic residue classes.
We also determine exact Taylor radii for three addresses. The manuscript retains the complete earlier
arithmetic, lifting, deformation, and analytic-regularity development, with detailed mathematical
appendices. A separate appendix states the precise remaining simplicity problem for ordinary
Euler tails. Formal coverage is explicit: the external conjecture and several four-address results
have inherited Lean verification; the new factorial, mixed-step, all-rank, and radius arguments are
written proofs with recorded audits and exact computational checks, and await dedicated Lean
formalization.

1 Scope and conventions
The central objects are sequences and polynomial equations equipped with arithmetic coordinates.
Residue projectors select addresses in a sequence, finite differences measure compatibility between
nearby addresses, and valuation bounds control the passage from finite precision to a p-adic limit.
These constructions provide a common language for the Euler packet results and the later lifting results.
Each theorem nevertheless retains its own coefficient ring, topology and nonsingularity hypotheses.
The arithmetic framework is developed together with its completed extensions. The stated external
Nishibuchi conjecture is proved in its full specified parameter range. The dyadic refinements and
polynomial deformation theorems give stronger conclusions under the hypotheses stated with each
result. The native conjectures retain their original identifiers, 13.2 and 13.3, when discussed as research
questions, although the section numbering of this consolidated manuscript is new.

Reading scope
Residual forests describe deformation above a fixed residual root. The later constructions compare
compatible families and recover summands inside supplied carriers. Universal companion existence,
carrier existence, and nonzero occupancy require additional inputs. Section D assembles the conditional
result and states those inputs explicitly.
Abstract
A residual representation is a genuine zeroth-order coordinate. All positive-depth perturbations
above it may fill its formal deformation neighborhood, but they cannot move into a different
residual class. This paper develops the corresponding universal object: a residual forest whose
roots are residual representations, whose finite levels are lifts modulo powers of a uniformizer, and
whose infinite branches are complete characteristic-zero objects. We prove the residual partition, no-
crossing, inverse-limit reconstruction, finite-branch compactness, exact smooth and singular branch
counts, packet decomposition of tangent and obstruction cohomology, a directed minimum-seed
theorem, rational seed-zeta formulas, and finite companion-forest completion. The coefficient prime
two is represented by a weighted forest in which characteristic-zero packets may merge modulo two
and become visible only at later depth. We then define a prime-independent system seed through
a common Frobenius spine, prove a compatible-carrier summand theorem under finite Frobenius
separation, and reduce finite occupancy in a fixed semisimple carrier to the nonnegative integer
trace of an exact joint projector. The paper does not prove that every admissible residual companion
exists or that every finite Hecke packet is occupied. Those two existence statements remain the exact
horizontal boundary beyond vertical deformation theory.

Abstract. Let K be a nonarchimedean local field. We resolve several finite layers that occur inside the local
Langlands correspondence for general linear groups. Frobenius semisimple Weil Deligne parameters first
split into irreducible Weil atoms and finite monodromy chains. In the tame case, character projectors show
that every irreducible atom is one transitive Frobenius orbit, and Mackey theory gives an exact greatest
common divisor and least common multiple rule for tensor packets. Regular finite field characters produce
primitive cuspidal projectors and finite Gauss phases. For wild data, projective intertwiners recover an
alternating commutator form. Its radical free quotient determines a finite Heisenberg representation, and
maximal isotropic averaging gives an exact selector. We prove a restricted one break bridge: an equivariant
symplectic isometry between a declared Galois envelope and a type side quotient induces the Heisenberg
comparison uniquely up to scalar, while one cyclic phase condition removes the remaining ambiguity. Odd
residue characteristic is governed by finite Weil phases. Residue characteristic two requires a quadratic
refinement and its Arf invariant. A matrix holonomy theorem then gives the exact gluing criterion on
a finite transport graph. The general arithmetic packet realization is stated as Conjecture 66. Detailed
ordinary proofs give restricted arithmetic realizations in all odd prime-power ranks and in all dyadic
ranks for the stated increasing-break families. The complete comparison of pair local factors remains a
conditional input for the same arithmetic candidate.

1 Introduction
The local Langlands correspondence for GLn(K) is an established theorem. It matches irreducible
smooth representations of GLn(K) with Frobenius semisimple Weil Deligne representations of
dimension n. Its proof and normalization draw on global methods, harmonic analysis, types, local
factors, and the geometry of Shimura varieties [19, 17, 8]. The present article asks a narrower structural
question. Which parts of the local correspondence admit finite packet coordinates whose projectors,
transfers, phases, and gluing laws can be proved directly?
The answer has a sharp division. The tame layers are explicit. A tame irreducible Weil representation
is induced from a character of an unramified extension. Its inertia restriction is one Frobenius orbit.

Bushnell and Henniart [4, 5, 6, 7, 9].

ABSTRACT. Let ¯ρ be a residual Galois representation and let R be a global deformation ring with declared
local conditions. We separate the global automorphy problem into residual occupancy, deformation
support, Hecke occupancy, and arithmetic realization. Local conditions are encoded by quotient rings
rather than by idempotents, since irreducible components of a local deformation ring need not be clopen.
For an ordinary or derived patching datum, full support descends through the augmentation quotient.
Near faithfulness is shown to be equivalent to full support for finite modules over Noetherian rings. An
isomorphism R ∼= T transports support, Fitting ideals, and point fibers, but a quotient map can erase
an entire component. Finite Hecke algebras are resolved into canonical Artin packets, so simultaneous
generalized eigenspaces are available without assuming semisimplicity. Nested packets in one finite carrier
stabilize; for changing finite carriers, nonzero stable cores give compatible inverse limit vectors. These
results give a pointwise criterion: a characteristic zero deformation point in automorphic support produces
a Hecke eigensystem. With attached Galois representations, local global compatibility, and classicality, the
point is automorphic. A fixed compatible system then propagates the conclusion to every coefficient place.
For finite coefficient quotients, compatible conjugacy classes admit compatible continuous representatives.
Declared polynomial quotient conditions survive their adic reconstruction. These completion statements
require explicit finite occupancy, continuity, and integral Frobenius data. Universal companion existence
and unrestricted reciprocity are not proved.

The present article does not replace those theorems. It isolates the algebraic support statements that
explain exactly what a patching package supplies once its arithmetic hypotheses have been verified.
The first correction concerns local packets. A local deformation ring is usually complete and local. Its
irreducible components are rarely open and closed. They cannot generally be represented by central
idempotents. The correct object is a quotient ring defining a local condition, together with the support
of a module or complex on the resulting spectrum. Central idempotents reappear later, where they
belong, inside finite Artin Hecke algebras and finite dimensional characteristic zero carriers.
The second correction concerns patching. The useful global conclusion is full support, often expressed
as near faithfulness. For a finite module over a Noetherian ring, near faithfulness is equivalent to
full support. Full support descends through the quotient that removes the auxiliary variables. This
statement is elementary, but it is the exact bridge from a patched module to componentwise occupancy
at finite level. The same conclusion holds for perfect complexes through derived support.
The third correction concerns Hecke packets. Semisimplicity is not required to isolate a maximal
Hecke packet. Every finite commutative algebra over a field is a product of Artin local algebras. Its
canonical central idempotents project onto simultaneous generalized eigenspaces. Trace is only a
secondary criterion in characteristic z

missing module vector is created by this relabeling.
An extra presentation generator changes nothing
Replacing diag(x, y) by diag(x, y, 1) adds a generator killed by the relation 1. The new maximal minor is xy, and
the new next-size minors generate (xy, x, y) = (x, y). The module and its intrinsic Fitting ideals are unchanged.
This is a small visible instance of presentation independence of Fitting ideals.
Read this as: Specialization substitutes into the actual relation matrix. An isomorphism transports all the
data. Neither operation may be replaced by an informal edit of the support picture.
